messages.subject: clustering error
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,

I’m having troubles with an error in openCR 1.4.1. I would really appreciate if anyone could give me some tips on fixing this error. I’ve already tried reinstalling R and updating all packages. Normally this code works great. But now I’m having a “cluster” issue. No errors in read.capthist. No errors in plotting my shapefile or traps and tracks. I’m at a complete loss.

Thanks,

Cheryl

messages.subject: Estimating abundance in multisession SECR using region.N
messages.subject_clean: Estimating abundance in multisession SECR using region.N
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have a multi-site SECR model that I am using to estimate snow leopard population densities and abundance. I am using the best fit spatial covariate model for reporting densities and abundances.

When I try to use the region.N function to estimate abundance from this multi-site model, I get this error:

region.N(best_mod, covmask.list, pooled.RN = TRUE)
Error in sumDpdot(object, sessnum, regionmask, D, noneuc, cellsize, constant = FALSE,  :
  dims [product 27300] do not match the length of object [33720]

## Removing the pooled.RN argument gives me estimates for each session.
region.N(best_mod, covmask.list)
[[1]]
    estimate SE.estimate      lcl      ucl n
E.N 20.84802    3.724021 14.73023 29.50666 2
R.N 18.70105         NaN      NaN      NaN 2

[[2]]
    estimate SE.estimate     lcl      ucl n
E.N 16.90213    3.290729 11.5813 24.66752 1
R.N 15.79853         NaN     NaN      NaN 1

[[3]] and so on.....

What is the best way to estimate abundance for the entire region of interest?

Many thanks,
Manvi

messages.subject: Re: clustering error
messages.body_plain:
A similar error was reported on phidot http://www.phidot.org/forum/viewtopic.php?f=36&t=3982#p13176
The OP hasn't come back on that, so I don't know if it was resolved. The problem is in join() that is called by openCR.fit() if the user has not pre-processed the data into the required form. Troubleshoot by calling join() yourself. I don't know at this stage whether there is a bug.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
I can't tell whether this is a limitation in 'secr' or an error in your setup. 'abundance' as you use the term is generally a nonsense parameter, especially with spatial covariate models that extrapolate outside the immediate area of the detectors.
Murray

messages.body_plain:
Rebecca
I think you're right that this is not something you can do with 'secr' as it stands. In retrospect the code should have allowed animal-specific parameter values, but it was written a long time ago and I hesitate to mess with it. However, I am part way to generating some standalone R code, if you can wait a day or two... On the question of how much it matters - will depend on trap saturation etc. so hard to say, and I don't see a reliable ad hoc fix.
Murray

messages.subject: Estimating a trend from a multisession model with empty sessions
messages.subject_clean: Estimating a trend from a multisession model with empty sessions
messages.body_plain:
Hi
I know one can enter an empty session for use in a multi-session model (by entering a dummy row for the session). Would one also need to include an empty trap object so that the model does not "think" that there was a sampling session that produced no captures which would affect say a detection function parameter that is common across sessions. I want to estimate a trend in density where I have data from different years but with some gaps i.e. no data from certain years.

Thanks!

Greg
